activity.text_alternative: Propagation delay is the time a signal takes to travel from one end of a link to the other; it depends on cable length and signal speed. Transmission delay is the time needed to transmit a packet; it depends on packet size and link transmission rate. Cable length belongs with signal travel, not packet transmission.
guided_steps: Trace the cable-length connection. Which delay depends on distance traveled?
Trace the packet-size and transmission-rate connection. If both stay unchanged, does that delay change?

nodes.label: Packet size and link transmission rate
Transmission delay: time to transmit the packet

edges.label: Longer cable increases delay; faster signal reduces it
Larger packet increases delay; higher rate reduces it

activity.text_alternative: Transmission delay is the time needed to transmit a packet, not instantaneous placement of all its bits onto the cable. It depends on packet size and link transmission rate. Propagation delay is the signal's travel time along the cable; it depends on cable length and signal speed. These are distinct contributions to latency.
guided_steps: Trace the inputs to transmission delay. If packet size and transmission rate stay unchanged, does making the cable longer change either input?

activity.text_alternative: A message travels from the starting host to the other host. This outward journey is one-way latency. A reply then travels from the other host back to the starting host. Round-trip time covers travel to the other end and back; it does not stop at the outward arrival. Both are measured in time.
guided_steps: Follow the outward message. At which host does this one-way journey end?
Follow the reply. At which host does the round trip end?
